outputs.L3:
A pneumatic tire includes a tread portion, a pair of sidewall portions extending inward in the tire radial direction from both edges of the tread portion, and bead portions provided at the radially inner ends of the sidewall portions.

The tread portion is provided with a center main groove and a shoulder main groove. Both the center main groove and the shoulder main groove extend continuously in the tire circumferential direction. A land portion is defined between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove.

The center main groove has a zigzag configuration as it extends in the tire circumferential direction. This zigzag shape may contribute to improved traction performance and drainage while maintaining rigidity in the adjacent land portion.

In the land portion, a plurality of lug grooves and discontinuous narrow grooves are formed. The lug grooves extend from the shoulder main groove toward the center main groove but terminate before reaching the center main groove. Each lug groove has an end portion located on the center-main-groove side, and this end portion is bent. The discontinuous narrow grooves are also provided in the land portion and are arranged so as not to extend continuously across the entire land portion.

With this configuration, the land portion between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove is provided with a groove arrangement that can enhance road contact performance, drainage, and edge effect, while the termination of the lug grooves before the center main groove helps maintain the rigidity of the land portion.
outputs.L4:
A pneumatic tire tread design is provided in which the tread portion is formed with a plurality of circumferential grooves and land portions arranged to improve running performance on both dry and wet road surfaces. The tread includes a center main groove extending continuously in the tire circumferential direction while following a zigzag path, and a shoulder main groove disposed outwardly of the center main groove in the tire width direction. Between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove, an intermediate land portion is defined.

The intermediate land portion is provided with a plurality of lug grooves extending inwardly from the shoulder main groove toward the center main groove. These lug grooves are arranged at intervals in the tire circumferential direction and are shaped so that their inner terminal ends are bent in the tire circumferential direction. The bent terminal end portions do not directly open into the center main groove, thereby limiting direct communication between the shoulder main groove and the center main groove. This structure helps prevent excessive reduction in the rigidity of the intermediate land portion while still allowing the lug grooves to contribute to drainage and edge effect.

In addition, narrow circumferential grooves are formed in the intermediate land portion. These narrow grooves extend generally in the tire circumferential direction but are discontinuous, rather than forming a fully continuous groove. Each narrow circumferential groove may be positioned so as to communicate with or approach the bent terminal portions of the lug grooves. By forming the narrow grooves discontinuously, the tread maintains sufficient land rigidity while providing additional biting edges and controlled water flow paths.

The zigzag configuration of the center main groove increases the number of edge components acting in the lateral direction, thereby improving traction and braking performance. The shoulder main groove contributes to drainage and enhances resistance to hydroplaning, while the inwardly extending lug grooves assist in discharging water from the intermediate region of the tread toward the outer side of the tire. Because the lug grooves terminate in bent end portions and do not fully cut across the intermediate land portion, excessive movement or deformation of the land portion during cornering and braking is suppressed.

As a result, the tread pattern achieves a balanced combination of grip, stability, drainage, and wear resistance. The controlled communication between the grooves improves wet performance without sacrificing tread block rigidity. The discontinuous narrow circumferential grooves further enhance traction and reduce uneven wear by distributing stress more uniformly through the intermediate land portion. Accordingly, the tire provides improved handling stability, reliable road contact, and favorable wear characteristics over a wide range of driving conditions.

counterfactuals.output:
A pneumatic tire includes a tread portion provided with a center main groove extending continuously in a tire circumferential direction in a zigzag manner, and a shoulder main groove disposed outward of the center main groove in a tire axial direction and extending continuously in the tire circumferential direction. A land portion is defined between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove.

The land portion is provided with a plurality of lug grooves spaced apart in the tire circumferential direction. Each lug groove extends from the shoulder main groove toward the center main groove and terminates within the land portion without opening into the center main groove. A terminal end portion of each lug groove is bent toward one side in the tire circumferential direction, thereby forming a bent terminal portion.

The land portion is further provided with a plurality of narrow grooves having a groove width smaller than that of the lug grooves. Each narrow groove extends in the land portion independently of the bent terminal portion of the corresponding lug groove. The narrow grooves are arranged so as not to be connected to the bent terminal portions of the lug grooves, thereby maintaining a separated rubber portion between each narrow groove and the adjacent bent terminal portion.

With this configuration, the zigzag center main groove contributes to drainage and edge effect near the tire equator, while the shoulder main groove secures circumferential drainage on the shoulder side. The lug grooves provide lateral drainage and traction edges in the land portion, and their bent terminal portions increase edge components in the circumferential direction. Since the narrow grooves are not connected to the bent terminal portions, excessive reduction in rigidity of the land portion is suppressed, improving wear resistance, steering stability, and resistance to block deformation while maintaining wet performance.
